label: r2c2
name: realign + more updates
hypothesis: Same network as c1; only the recipe changes: 128 envs x 16 steps, 8 minibatches, 3 PPO epochs. This gives about 1.3x more samples (about 170k steps) and about 83 updates instead of 32, so the policy has more chances to learn rewarding placements before DONE dominates. Refuted if dev success is not above c1 by more than seed noise (about 5 points), or if it falls below c1.
last_analysis: Undoing the observed X/2 column roll took dev success from 0 to 0.47, and r2c2's recipe (128 envs, 8 minibatches, 3 epochs) raised it to 0.715 on both seeds. Every change in round 3 lost ground: 64 envs, 2 epochs and a deeper trunk. All three had one seed at 0.000 and the other at 0.15–0.51. So the main problem is seed instability or collapse, not capacity or sample count. One collapse type: r3c1 seed 0 used only 1x1 bricks. Remaining errors in the traces are wrong-layer placements and stopping with DONE one brick short. For the last round I keep r2c2 and make one change per candidate: (A) near-uniform initial policy logits (small-gain output layers), so early exploration is unbiased; (B) a larger entropy bonus to resist collapse; (C) a longer horizon (gamma 0.99, lambda 0.95), so the +1 exact-build bonus outweighs per-step shaping and wrong-layer errors cost more.
